findings.reason: §16's own done-when censuses callers of `read_plan_review(` and requires none in recovery (already true) but does not mention these two, so the plan should name and repoint them (or state why their question differs from coverage) to keep one owner of the coverage question.
findings.text: §16 establishes `plan_review._review_coverage` as "the gate's one owner of the coverage question" and section-keys the digest, but two other call sites still answer the same "which review covers this plan" question through the whole-document reader `read_plan_review(project, slug)` (`reckon/mcp.py:4324` in the plan-review view, `reckon/cli.py:2613` in the answer verb), neither named or repointed by §16 or §23; after §16 a plan covered section-wise but not whole-document reads as unreviewed at these two readers while the gate admits it, the exact drift §15 was written to close

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each open section hides substantial behaviour behind one small interface: §16 extends the private `_review_coverage` predicate over two existing readers (`list_plan_reviews`, `implementable_sections`) plus `section_prose`; §22 keeps the threshold, the done-when locator, the declaration comparison and the word-diff measure private to `plan_review.py`; §23 exposes one public `store_delivered_reviews` over the moved loop and private `write_review_sidecar`.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 names the coverage question's owner but does not census the other readers that answer it; see FINDING.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 accounts for its one net public definition (`section_prose`, with the interim `strip_tags` retired to private), §21 states no public definition is added, §22 adds `plan_review_settings` and retires `plan_review_settle_seconds`, and §23 adds `store_delivered_reviews` and retires `store_delivered_report` to private; no section adds a CLI option (the answer verb's `--answer` already exists at `reckon/cli.py:2587`) or an MCP view, and §16/§23 state no refusal family is added.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design sections cite the machinery they extend, checking against the code rather than asserting it: `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` and `structured_section_spans`/`plan_headings` on `reckon/_plan_html.py`, `_TAG_RE`/`_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS` and `count_open_decisions` (verified `reckon/_plan_html.py:1876-1910`), `roadmap.implementable_sections` (`reckon/roadmap.py:107`), `list_plan_reviews`, `review_report_directory`/`delivered_reports`/`store_delivered_report` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:786-946`), `dispatch._normalised_words`/`_longest_contiguous_word_span` (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:289,477`) and `flight.plan_review_settle_seconds` (`reckon/flight.py:684`). A spot-check of the two "plan-review" root spellings (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:795,866`) and the `get_text`/`stripped_strings` census (fourteen lines, all classified) matches the plan's account.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two additions that cross a boundary are justified moves, not parallel layers: §23 moves the existing `routing._store_delivered_plan_review` loop beside `store_delivered_report` (which it retires to private), and §21 factors the duplicate plan-review report root into one private function rather than adding a second path builder.
